name: Divider
summary: Hairline rule that separates content. Horizontal (most common) or vertical (toolbar separator). Optional inline label for section breaks ('OR'). Decorative by default (role='presentation'); use role='separator' when the divider has semantic meaning (between menu groups, between toolbar groups).

label.description: Optional inline label rendered in the middle ('OR', 'and 12 more', 'Last week'). Always paired with horizontal orientation.

weight.description: Maps to border.hairline / subtle / default / strong. hairline is the operator default; strong is for hero / marketing section breaks.

decorative.description: When false, sets role='separator' with proper aria-orientation. Use when the divider has SR semantic meaning (between Menu groups, between Toolbar groups).

inset.description: Horizontal margin inset, common in lists ('inset divider' pattern from iOS — list rows separator skips the leading 56 px to align with text).

rules: Semantic dividers (between menu groups, toolbar groups) set role='separator' and aria-orientation.

Hairline contrast is intentionally low (~1.2:1 on canvas) — at decorative weight this is correct (WCAG 1.4.11 applies to non-text content that conveys meaning; pure decoration is exempt). For semantic separators bump to weight='default' or 'strong'.

do: Default to hairline for in-list and in-section separation.
Use label='OR' between form sections that present alternative paths ('Use a passkey OR continue with a password').
Use inset='lg' on list rows where the leading content is an avatar / icon — the divider aligns under the text, not under the avatar.
Use vertical dividers inside Toolbars and Navbars to group related actions.
dont: Don't stack two visible weights (hairline + default) on the same surface. Pick one.
Don't paint dividers in lime — chrome, not action.
Don't use Divider as a structural border on Cards — Cards bring their own border.
Don't use Divider for vertical centering tricks — use Stack / Spacer.

changelog.note: Initial Divider contract. Horizontal / vertical. Optional inline label. Four weights. Inset modes for list rows.
